claims.title: Exact sample reuse: target-query floor and solved large-batch minimax regime

quoted_fields.interface: Known finite alphabet [d], d>=2; integer m>=1 and rational 0<eta<=1/8. Fixed UNKNOWN laws P,Q, ACTUAL old IID archive X~P^m, and only independent opaque named P/Q sample queries plus fair bits. One distribution-independent program must halt almost surely with finite fair-bit computation and output the ENTIRE exact law Q^m for every pair. No probability/density evaluation, shared source seed, distribution-dependent advice, timing/identity access to the opaque oracle, or old Q-dependent side information. Query-floor theorem does not require a retention guarantee. Minimax C* additionally requires expected same-row changed fraction<=TV(P,Q)+eta.
quoted_fields.failure: Only the large-batch regime m>=ceil((d-1)/eta^2) has the exact minimax value m. Full smaller-batch/all-log rate remains OPEN; max{m,C1-m+1} is a lower bound, not a matched universal rate. Do not multiply the one-record tolerant-testing lower bound by m; its transfer subtracts the m-1 newly acquired old-law records and retains its original asymptotic small-eta conditions/unknown constants. No atom floor, exponential moment or deterministic total-call cap is silently assumed in the target floor. Classical stopped change of measure/Wald/data processing is imported; ROOT explicitly derives the one-way absolute-continuity extension at degenerate Q rather than misapplying a mutual-AC lemma. Existing empirical matching and N1691/Dots/DDB1/SCC operations count once. No new implementation, independent audit, priority, discovery score or acquired practical advantage. Unknown-law source access is essential; known target probabilities/advice are different contracts. All source/access/ZIP/resource holds remain; no held original was retried or recovered.
